SABRENT 10 Port 60W USB 3.0 Hub with Individual Power Switches and LEDs Includes 60W 12V/5A Power Adapter (HB-BU10) My current laptop is over eight (8) years old; and as usual – parts fails.

I rely on my USB ports quite a bit – external mouse, phone (as I also use it as a camera), charging/syncing my iPod, USB/flash/thumb drives for back-up storage. With only three (3) USB ports on my laptop, and two of them not working, I needed a HUB.

This was within the price range, and manageable. It was given to me last year as a gift and I haven’t gone a day without it. I hooked it up to the good port, hooked up my external mouse and it’s been great. I’ve been able to slow charge and/or sync my Samsung GS8, charge/sync my iPod, and sync my flash drives.

I enjoy the “power” on/off switches on the hub so that the ports aren’t always being used.

The hub is small enough to fit on my desk, my purse, or laptop bag. It is easy to use – plug into the computer/laptop port, plug the other (mouse, etc) in, turn on the hub, good to go. The cord is a bit short, though depending on where you're using it that could be both a blessing or annoyance.

I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend this or buy another one.
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT 10 Port 60W USB 3.0 Hub with Individual Power Switches and LEDs Includes 60W 12V/5A Power Adapter (HB-BU10)

text_fidelity_a: Tile Mate (2016) - 1 Pack - Discontinued by Manufacturer The title is good at doing what it does, that being said, it's not a complete life changer. I bought both the wallet and key finder for someone who loses everything everywhere. It's very convenient when the item is simply lost in the house. I believe it would be nicer if everyone in the world used a tile so that the software would be able to constantly locate a missing item but that's just not the case. However, we did lose a wallet in someone's car after being dropped off at home. The app last located the item at the house which was the last time the phone and wallet were together. After asking the person to look in there car, they were unable to find it. But one day when the phone was near that same car it was able to pick up the signal coming from the tile and we ended up finding it wedged deep down between the seats. That being said, if someone were to steal your item, it's probably not going to help but the way the tile works in telling you its last location is super useful.
text_fidelity_b: Tile Mate (2016) - 1 Pack - Discontinued by Manufacturer

ICE COOREL Laptop Cooling Pad with 6 Cooling Fans, Laptop Fan Cooling Pad for 14-17 Inch, Gaming Laptop Cooler Stand with 6 Height Adjustable, Notebook Cooler Pad with Two USB Port [2022 Version] [[VIDEOID:810a58277a7c88ee7b3cf4de0da31205]] I have a fair amount of experience with laptops that get hot to the point i have software on my laptop that helps me keep track of core temperatures. I've tried a couple different cooling pads and this is by far my favorite. I'm using it as I type this with my 17" LG Gram.

The bottom can be adjusted so that the laptop sits flat or at different angles. There are two flip up tabs that can be used to keep the laptop positoned. When they're up, they are about a quarter inch above the base of the laptop and some people might notice them more depending on the angle of the arm and the wrist but I don't notice them at all.

The dial on the side adjusts the fan; it is extremely quiet even at highest speed. I can feel the cool air when i put my hand at the side of the pad and to some extent, i can feel it on my legs -- which might be a slight issue on a cold winter night but I'll live with that.

My only complaint is that when I've set it down and pick it up to move back to my lap. the bar holding the pad at an angle can come loose if i'm not careful to pickit up by the very bottom of the pad and not the part that's flush to the laptop. I'll probably adjust to that with continued use.

Very pleased with this pad! Would highly recommend!
text_fidelity_b: ICE COOREL Laptop Cooling Pad with 6 Cooling Fans, Laptop Fan Cooling Pad for 14-17 Inch, Gaming Laptop Cooler Stand with 6 Height Adjustable, Notebook Cooler Pad with Two USB Port [2022 Version]

text_fidelity_a: Meffort Inc Laptop Skin Sticker Cover Art Decal Decorative Stickers Fits Laptop up to 17.3 Inch (Included 2 Wrist Pads) - Green Heart Butterfly Went shopping for a laptop skin and checked all the usual places then came to Amazon.  One of these days I will learn to just come here first and save myself some time!  I ordered this skin after reading the reviews here, figured that for the price I would not be out too much if it was not the best quality.  Pleasant surprise!  Not only did the laptop skin and matching mouse pad arrive before the delivery date, but they were well packed and arrived without wrinkles or damage.  The skin is heavy weight and has a texture to it, but it does not impact the design at all.  The back of the skin has cutting lines for you to cut to fit your laptop.  The skin cut easily with a scissors, leaving a nice clean edge.  My laptop measures 15 x 13 so I had to cut the skin down a bit, but the design remained largely unaffected.  The back pealed off easily, and the skin attached to the laptop without any issue at all.  It seems sticky enough to hold well and take some abuse without peeling off any time soon - but it did lift easy on the initial application to allow for a repositioning without any issue at alll. text_fidelity_a:
Manfrotto 3-Way Pan/Tilt Head with RC2 Quick Release Plate (MH804-3WUS) I am writing one review for my entire purchase - it just makes sense that you know about the entire setup.

I bought the Manfrotto 808RC4 along with their 190XPROB Pro Tripod and the Manfrotto MB MSTRAP-1 Tripod Carrying Strap. All at Amazon. Here's why:

This head gives you unlimited control in all directions. The large knurled handles allow you to grip and adjust the tension on the pivot points to any degree you want. I use it to pan video, I use it to do off center composure and metering. I love how rock steady this thing is when I am shooting my 60and 120 second exposures with my 300MM lens. Rock steady. And the rotation is greased smooth, nary a glitch.

With a bubble level and two straight levels you always know where you are. And gradients to indicate -30 to +90 tilt for replication. Great for panning video or shooting stills for a panorama. There are two "softening springs" to slow the movement of the tilts as you reach either end. You can disengage them if you wish.

I have friends that went with the ball heads. And regret it. They are fast, but not accurate, especially with a long lens. With this head you can adjust the tension and just ease the camera around without having to adjust it again.

Now hear me on this. I see other reviewers not so happy with the way the shoe is a little tricky. Let me say that by practicing with the shoe mounted to your camera and paying close attention snap it onto the head three times and you know all you need to know. You may have to practice a few more times to get it in the dark but I tell you that you are going to love it. When you snap the camera onto the head it automatically engages and you have no worries. The double safety has stopped me from dropping my camera twice. Lesson learned at no cost.

As to the tripod - sturdy is the word that comes to mind. And NOT overly weighty. Together the head and tripod are 7 lbs. With the strap - which I did not buy at first - this rig is rock solid and you won't even know you are carrying it. I don't even notice the combo. I hike several hours at a time and have been know to stop in a panic on the way out and feel on my back to see if the whole thing is still there! I think a big part of the "weight" issue is how it is carried. In your hands it feels hefty. On your hips, 7 lbs feels weighty. Across your shoulder diagonally, head down? It ain't even there!

The tripod has a wonderfully steady center column assembly that comes up and tilts over to the horizontal - great for macro shots or simply needing to place the camera where you aren't. The legs are sturdy and the snap retainers have just the right tension - not too hard to snap open or closed, not so loose that you worry whether one might slide. I also like that the center column is not attached to the legs with the typical arms of lesser well made tripods. Makes for very easy folding and stowing. I love the leg angle presets - easy to use and not worried about them slipping. The rubber grips on two of the legs are a hand saver in chilly weather. Nice touch.

So, in case you haven't figured it out, I love this rig. If I were going trekking across country for days I might want a little less weight, but for day long trips, portraiture or car trips this is the ticket.
text_fidelity_b: Manfrotto 3-Way Pan/Tilt Head with RC2 Quick Release Plate (MH804-3WUS)

text_fidelity_a:
Creative Sound Blaster Roar 2 Portable NFC Bluetooth Speaker with aptX/AAC (Black) I’m a big fan of the Roar since it provides me with two key benefits: great sound and is easy to use. The Roar 2 retains those two benefits and adds one more: a smaller footprint. I’m going to try my best to not overuse the words “outstanding” and "impressive" in this review, but it’s going to be a challenge. This is an impressive speaker.

The out-of-the-box experience is nicely done. As expected at this price point, it comes in upscale packaging. More important, it comes with a pretty decent user guide. That’s significant since the Roar 2 has a lot of features – to call it just “a speaker” really shortchanges it. It’s also a recorder, a power bank, an MP3 player, an SD card reader, a speakerphone – it will even lull you to sleep with Bedtime Mode where it gradually decreases the volume and then powers off. My only complaint about the manual is that it’s physically small, which means the type size is also small. I do wish manufacturers would realize that those of us with aging eyes still like loud music!

And loud music is this product’s forte. I’m able to get room-filling sound while maintaining crisp highs, clear midrange and solid but not muddy bass. I can even go past room-filling to the “let’s annoy the neighbors” levels and still maintain impressive fidelity. Using the Tera Bass option boosts the bass response to the point where you would swear there was a separate subwoofer on the floor. You can see the end plates resonate to help drive the bass (plus it just looks really cool as well).

Day to day usage of the Roar 2 is straightforward even though there are so many features. All the buttons are labeled fairly clearly, albeit at times with small type. I would also have preferred a greater contrast to the labels since sometimes they are hard to see unless the Roar 2 is under a bright light. There are voice prompts for many key features which I found helpful. Normally I don’t care for voice prompts, but these were done in a natural sounding voice at a low volume making them not at all irritating. But, if you don’t like them at all, you can turn them off. There are small, but clear indicator lights to keep you apprised of battery charge level, settings, and other criteria.

The build quality is excellent. This feels as good as it looks, with a solid heft to it, an excellent quality metal grill, and quality plastic case components. All the buttons have a good tactile feel to them. I have it in white, which looks very nice with the gray contrast control pad. My only quibble is that some of the buttons/levers are on the small side. However, those tend to be the lesser used function. The main function buttons (on/off, volume, pairing, Tera Bass, etc.) are larger and easy to use.

The Roar 2 is not inexpensive, but the performance, build quality and features make it an excellent value. If you enjoy great sound and need to keep to a small footprint speaker, these should absolutely be on your short list (and at the top of it by a wide margin). Highly, highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Creative Sound Blaster Roar 2 Portable NFC Bluetooth Speaker with aptX/AAC (Black)

text_fidelity_a: Lenovo Chromebook C330 2-in-1 Convertible Laptop, 11.6" HD Display, MediaTek MT8173C, 4GB RAM, 64GB Storage, Chrome OS, Blizzard White Chromebook prices range from around $100 to over $1000. Better Chromebooks have Intel Core CPUs for great performance. The much cheaper Mediatek system in this Chromebook gives it mediocre performance, especially for intensive games or for business users who open lots of tabs simultaneously and frequently switch between them. On the plus side this Chromebook has a useful 4GB of RAM, a sharp colorful IPS screen, a touch screen that works great with Android apps, a very responsive (for swiping) touchpad, and reliable WiFi (much better than my HP laptop). On the minus side, the white plastic shell looks and feels a little cheap, the screen is not very bright, and the touchpad's button feels a little clunky. In summary, if you can't afford more than $300, this is a good choice for casual users who only have a few tabs open at once and use it mostly for email, Facebook, web surfing, and streaming music or videos. If you can afford $350 to $400, you will have several choices with more powerful CPUs for more intensive users.

text_fidelity_a:
Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black) Though I use Windows XP, my computer is old and my processor (Sempron) is not what is required to run the "KODAK Share Button" app to transfer videos from the Kodak Playful, Model Ze2 to my computer. That's too bad. But anyway, be sure to check the specs before buying so this won't happen to you. I downloaded the program anyway but it wouldn't run. So, I've tried just about everything I know to do and nothing seems to work. An old "FinePixViewer" program keeps popping up every time I try to download a video, but it takes a very long time for it to finally work. I guess technology is trying to force me to buy a newer/faster computer because so many gadgets won't work on poor ole' Bessie anymore despite her having 34 GB left of memory and 4GB of ram.

The camera itself is fun to play with and I like the 1970's film mode, but it would be better if the theme to "Shaft" was being quietly played in the background while using that particular mode. The access doors are very difficult to open and you will probably lose some fingernails until you get it figured out. The Kodak website is not very good.....I never could find a place where I could ask a question directly to technical support. And the web addresses provided in the manual take you to the same web page regardless of the the specifics written into the web address like: [...]. They all take you to the same place and you have to hunt and peck where you want to go and what you're looking for. And they have no Ze2 demos to watch - go figure. And though Windows XP is listed in a drop menu, when I click on it absolutely nothing happens. So much for Windows XP help.

I'm giving it 3 stars because the doors are a pain, and the website is inadequate. But since I don't own a computer that will allow the Kodak program to work I can't fairly judge the quality of the videos. When I can get FinePixView to play them they look alright. I have yet to connect the Kodak Playful directly to my HDTV to see how the HD (720) quality and sound are, and I will do that and report back. I am very interested especially in the sound quality since I'm a musician/music teacher and like to record my students playing.

UPDATE: 2.17.12
I used the Kodak Playful to record my daughter playing guitar in her school's talent show. It did a good job and I was finally able to upload the video to my old computer. Also, I ended up breaking off the door that covers the USB plug which was nearly impossible to open without losing fingernails and then equally impossible to shut close again. The plug stays inside without the door and though I hated doing it, it works much better now.
text_fidelity_b: Kodak PlayFull ZE2 Waterproof Video Camera with 2x Optical Zoom and 2-Inch LCD Screen (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR WiFi Mesh Range Extender EX6400 - Coverage up to 2100 sq.ft. and 35 devices with AC1900 Dual Band Wireless Signal Booster & Repeater (up to 1900Mbps speed), plus Mesh Smart Roaming Works well if you can figure it out

I bought a Netgear EX6250 in a brick-and-mortar store about four months ago and my experience with it has been good overall...though not without its complications. Past experience with late-model Netgear products can be helpful in getting this unit set up and operating as the process is not always straightforward. It took me (who has a lot of experience with Netgear products and home networking in general) rather a few tries to get onto the right track in the Nighthawk app to set the thing up - you can run into roadblocks due to aspects of the Nighthawk app's design being less than intuitive (I know I did). I can't remember specifics now...so you know what I'm going to do? Out of lovingfriendliness for my fellow Amazon customers, I'm going to reset the extender to factory settings and set it back up, taking notes along the way, so that I can relate my experience more clearly and in greater detail.

Okay, so:

First you want to jump online and download the Netgear Nighthawk app to your phone. I don’t know if this unit can be set up without it.

Next, plug the extender into power - somewhere where it’s in range of your router. After you first plug the unit in, or after resetting it using the little recessed paperclip button on the side, the power LED will glow orange for rather a long time - two to three minutes in my experience - before finally turning green. Green means “go” - but orange doesn’t. So you just have to wait until that light turns green in order to be able to proceed with the setup process. Good opportunity to focus on the breath. And the fact that patience is a virtue.

Once the power indicator turns green, launch the Nighthawk app and check the little circle confirming that you accept Netgear’s terms and conditions and that you’ve read their privacy policy…even though you probably haven’t. Then tap “I Agree”.

On an iPhone, at least, the next screen says that iOS requires that you enable local network access in order to be able to set up your extender (which at this point the Nighthawk app is calling a “router” because it doesn’t yet know any better - you haven’t yet told it what you want to set up). Obviously, since you want to set up your extender, you’re going to okay that local network access. Tap “Continue” and your phone will ask you if you want to allow the app to find and connect to devices on your local network. Tap “OK”.

The next screen asks you to allow push notifications. This one’s up to you. I think I’ve always allowed them and I haven’t seen one yet, let alone been annoyed by excessive/unwanted notifications that are, in the end, just trying to sell me crap or otherwise waste my time.

The next screen tells you Netgear needs access to your device’s location services to automatically connect to your wifi network. I always allow this.

Next you’re told you have to create a new Netgear account or log into an existing one. Do that.

Then you’ll be asked if you want to enable Face ID and you’ll also be asked…something else I forget because I just blazed past it, momentarily forgetting that I was writing this detailed description of the process. But…y’know. You can read (because you’re reading this), so…tap the things on your screen that accord with your wishes. :)

At last we come to a screen that says, “Let’s set up your Nighthawk”, and tells you what to do if the unit’s been set up before. I don’t think I’ve ever had any luck using the “been set up before” option, so I always reset the extender to factory settings (by pressing and holding the paperclip/pen-point button on the side of the unit until the power light blinks orange) when I have a problem with the connection (which I seldom do, and when I do it’s usually because the power’s blinked or something else explicit has happened to make me need to set the extender up again). If this is your first time setting it up, tap “Set up a Nighthawk”. Even though I don’t think this extender is technically a Nighthawk. Doesn’t matter - you can still set it up with this app.

Next you’re shown a rundown of what’s going to happen. Read that as you’re inclined, then tap “Get Started!”.

On the product selection screen that comes up next, tap “Range Extender”.

The app tells you where to plug in your extender. Follow its instructions and tap “Next”.

The next screen just tells you to actually plug it in now, and wait (…and wait…and wait…) for a solid (green) power LED. Do that, and when you’ve got the solid green power light, tap “Next”.

On the next screen, the app will ask you to let it join your extender’s network. Tap “OK”, and wait while your phone connects to your extender. When it does, the screen will change to display “Great, we found your extender”. Tap “Next”.

Tap “Next” on the next screen as well.

Now your phone will look for your router’s network (which is your pre-existing wifi network, the one you want to extend). I think what it’s doing now is acting as a liaison between your router and the extender - introducing them to one another, as it were. Because what happens next is that your extender looks for and - ideally - connects to your wifi network. (When you’re asked to allow…something…to join your network, tap “Join”.)

And if all has gone well, that’s pretty much it. You’ll see a screen that says you’re up and running, and…there it is: you’re up and running!

Obviously, all of that is how things are *supposed* to go. If they go otherwise…you’ll probably need to be able to apply a searing laser beam of logic to the process and figure out how to make it work (that’s been my personal approach and, lucky for me, it’s always worked so far), or else to contact the dread Netgear Support People. I hope for your sake the laser beam works.

Good luck and enjoy!
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR WiFi Mesh Range Extender EX6400 - Coverage up to 2100 sq.ft. and 35 devices with AC1900 Dual Band Wireless Signal Booster & Repeater (up to 1900Mbps speed), plus Mesh Smart Roaming

text_fidelity_a:
Lenovo Legion Y720 Gaming Laptop, 15.6" Full HD, Intel Core i7-7700HQ Processor, 16GB DDR4 RAM, 512GB SSD, GeForce GTX 1060-6GB, Windows 10 Signature Image - 80VR0078US Like all dedicated gaming laptops, this is a big heavy high-powered machine. It is portable enough to lug over to your buddy's house for play dates, but it is too bulky and heavy to carry to work everyday. Construction is very good with an aggressive-looking aluminum case to match the aggressive-sounding "Legion" product name. Mechanical keyboard has decent (but not the best) travel and the large keys are backlit so you can easily play your games in the dark. Dolby Atmos audio works well for games, but is kind of thin for music or movies unless you hook it up to external speakers. This Y720 version has a 1080p IPS display, which is OK but not as bright or contrasty as some other laptops I have used. There is also a more expensive 4K display available, but I have not tried that.

Core i7 CPU with 16GB of RAm gives you really great performance. This machine is easily powerful enough for any games I tried on it. Even though performance is throttled somewhat when run off the battery, battery life is still less than 2 hours under heavy use (maybe 6 hours with light use).

For the money, it is hard to go wrong with these Lenovo Legions. If you don't want to spend more than $1000, the cheaper Legion Y520 is almost as good for most types of games and costs $300 less.
text_fidelity_b: Lenovo Legion Y720 Gaming Laptop, 15.6" Full HD, Intel Core i7-7700HQ Processor, 16GB DDR4 RAM, 512GB SSD, GeForce GTX 1060-6GB, Windows 10 Signature Image - 80VR0078US

HP Pavilion X360 14-Inch Convertible Laptop, Intel Core I5-8265U Processor, 8 GB RAM, 1 TB Hard Drive & 128 GB Solid-State Drive, Windows 10 Home (14-cd1042nr, Mineral Silver) It's not hyperbole for me to say I love this laptop. After working with glitchy, draggy old computers for the last year or so, this is a huge revelation for me. Not only is it fast on a task-to-task basis, but the startup and shutdown processes are incredibly fast. It's not wasting my time. Nor does it waste my time with a lot of bloatware. Yes there is some, but most is easy to remove should you not want it.

I like a smaller screen and keyboard, so this is perfect for me, and it's lightweight and has a slim profile, so it's easy to take along when I'm out and about. I love the way it converts to a tablet when you fold the screen back. Even the fingerprint recognition is dramatically better than anything I've had before. One thing I was skeptical about was the placement of the power button on the side. I was sure I'd be turning the laptop on or off accidentally, but I've discovered that it's not that simple, which is a load off my mind.

I could wish for a couple more USB ports particularly as I use both a wireless mouse and because there's no disk drive, so I have to attach an external one when I want to access files on disk. Eh, I'll survive it. There are always work-arounds.

Bottom line is that this laptop is a perfect match for me. I'm a writer (not a gamer) and this runs all the software I need, runs it fast and efficiently, and has tremendous storage capacity for all my files. I really couldn't have asked for more. Nicely done, HP.
text_fidelity_b: HP Pavilion X360 14-Inch Convertible Laptop, Intel Core I5-8265U Processor, 8 GB RAM, 1 TB Hard Drive & 128 GB Solid-State Drive, Windows 10 Home (14-cd1042nr, Mineral Silver)

- one full charge lasts several days
- good way to track your BPM, Blood pressure, calories burn, steps taken

- if you take the watch off for whatever reason (like to shower) it doesn't keep taking your BMP or blood pressure so you don't have to worry about your data getting messed up/ inaccurate.

dislike:

text_fidelity_a:
SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers With crime rates going up in NYC, this is an ideal kit for anyone living in an apartment, especially if they're alone and elderly. It covers two areas most vulnerable to thieves: your window and the door, while the key chain is best for when you're coming home late at night on a dark, lonely street. Just pull the pin and the alarm screams.

Of the three items, I would say the window alarm rates highest in terms of usefulness. In fact, I wish this set came with three of them. We travel a lot, and the biggest fear we have is intruders breaking in through our high-rise window, as we have a fire escape near one of them.

The door stop is the least useful to me as a thief would have to break through one of our windows first before going through a door. My front door is already secured by locks and the other doors in our place generally remain open. I suppose we could reinforce the front door with the doorstop, but it seems like overkill. If you lived in a dorm and wanted a particular room to be off-limits, I suppose it would be useful in that case. This item reminds me of the alarm that would be set off if you used an emergency exit. As if in acknowledgement that this item won't be used as much as the others, no battery was supplied for it, unlike the others.

As for the key chain, this is one of those devices that will lay dormant for long periods (knock on wood). You'll have to remember to check and test the batteries occasionally because it will be rarely used.

Overall, for the price this set can't be beat. It feels more like a "sampler" pack, though, as it has only one of each product when multiples of each one would have been more helpful.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Home Security Personal Safety Kit, Comes With A 120 dB Doorstop Alarm, 120 dB Door Or Window Alarm And A 120 dB Personal Alarm, Safety Essentials For College Students, Home Owners and Travelers

text_fidelity_a:
Munitio SV Mobile Performance Earphones with 3 Button Mic Control, Bronze Lower and mid end earphones have generally been lacking in both quality and performance. Given my propensity to misplace them, I have been reluctant to invest in more expensive versions. But with increased reliance on mobile devices, it was most definitely time to upgrade.

My familiarity with Munitio was more from their urban chic style complete with bullet motif, Kevlar coated cord, "tactical" carrying case and "hollow point" ear cups. At the risk of looking more Duck dynasty than cool, I was eager to try them.

Designed for use with Apple devices, the phones come securely packaged in a black carrying case. The look is sleek and modern and the bronze color is appealing. These are also available in black and gray. There are three sets of ear cups in different sizes. They were comfortable and shut out outside noise. The cord is flat and tangle free with a heft that promises durability. The 3 button mic control is located on the upper left hand side of the earphone cable. I really couldn't see the buttons but quickly mastered them by touch. They provide full functionality for calls and music on iPods, iPods and iPhones and just music for other mp3 players and Android devices.

I encountered no difficulties in making or taking calls. I could hear the other party and they could hear me without difficulty. The mic is positioned close enough to the mouth and is sufficiently sensitive that I didn't have to scream or repeat things. I made calls from a fairly busy coffee shop and a mall and ambient noise did not impair the call quality.

I tried these earphones with my IPod and a cheap mp3 player of dubious lineage. The sound was clear, strong and enjoyable. I did not find the bass overwhelming and was generally pleased with the performance.

Bottom line, I liked these earphones. The case and the trio of ear cups are thoughtful touches. Although light, there is a sense of substance and quality. The controls are intuitive and easy to use. There is a two year limited warranty. Serving up generous doses of comfort, convenience and performance, these ear phones are right on target.
text_fidelity_b: Munitio SV Mobile Performance Earphones with 3 Button Mic Control, Bronze

CalDigit TS3 Plus Thunderbolt 3 Dock - 85W Charging, 7X USB 3.1 Ports, USB-C Gen 2, DisplayPort, UHS-II SD Card Slot, LAN, Optical Out, for 2016+ MacBook Pro & PC (Silver - 0.7m/2.3ft Cable) This is unquestionably the best docking station for any MacBook that supports Thunderbolt 3. I have tried several other similar devices and they all had serious problems, while this provides 87W of power, dual display support (DisplayPort 1.2), both an analogue and digital audio (TOSLINK) device, SD card reader, and extra 5 Gbps Thunderbolt 3/USB-C and USB 3.0 ports.

Regarding the 1 star reviews, with the exception of the person with the defective unit, I am almost positive the problems people have been having are because of their cables. Most people don't realize that the white USB-B cable that comes with their MacBook (which they probably just use for power) is Thunderbolt 2 and will NOT support Thunderbolt 3 devices! To connect your computer to the dock, use the cable they provide. If you need a longer cable, be sure to buy an actual Thunderbolt 3 cable that is less than 2 meters long. As for your display cables, it is critical the cable is DisplayPort 1.2. I also connected the second monitor to the Thunderbolt 3 port that converted to DisplayPort 1.2 (I just got the Amazon Basics brand and it works as it should. I have used this on both my 2017 and 2019 MacBooks and they both work flawlessly. Its so nice to just have one cable to plug and unplug for all devices!

I must agree with many of the reviews: The build quality of this hardware is excellent. I believe it is well engineered and built. They include lots of hardware to help fit various TV's. I used this for my 42" Olevia LCD. I used the shortest screws of the proper thread size and pitch and also added own 1/4" Washer so the screws would not bottom out on the TV inserts. I also used Red Lock Tight on all hardware (lock washers were supplied and I did use them, but I have always been a Lock Tight user. The supplied lag screws and washers worked well for my wood stud walls (It is obviously ok, but they supplied 6 lags but there are only four (4) holes that can be used for studs on 16" centers. It would be nice if they added another hole for each side for an additional lag).

The price was fantastic. No box store could touch this price, nor adjust ability. I put this on the wall the day it arrived (Tuesday Aug 30th), so not even a week yet, so time will tell how it holds up.

Also, I did not get this very adjustable mount for constant or even occasional moving. We placed the TV in the corner of the room very high off the floor and a standard mount would not have allowed for this positioning.

The documentation was not the best, but was sufficient.
text_fidelity_b: Cheetah Mounts APDAM2B Articulating Dual Arm TV Wall Mount Bracket for 32 to 65-Inch LCD, LED, Plasma, Flat Screen Monitors Bundle with Twisted Veins 10-Feet HDMI Cable and 6-Inch Level

text_fidelity_a:
Cisco-Linksys WRT160N Wireless-N Broadband Router I was having terrible problems connecting to work from home over VPN. My MS communicator (IM) and Outlook just wouldn't work right over VPN. The help desk at work blamed by bandwidth and ISP (comcast). This didn't make sense since everyone nearly else at work also uses comcast and has the same bandwidth.

Many folks at work were also having issues with IM and said switching to a Linksys router fixed their isses - so I took the plunge. It did fix my IM. And, the wireless signal strength is better than before.

But, it didn't fix Outlook. Linksys and my IT help folks looked at it. I spent more time rebooting my computer in the past week than I could stand.

Outlook still would not work over my wireless but I could connect with no issues over my neighbors unsecured network. I called Comcast and they wanted to upgrade my modem's software but said the thing was soooo old it had to be replaced. A comcast guy was at my house by later in the day and replaced my modem in less than one hour - half of that on-hold waiting for the tech guy at comcast proper to pick up the phone so they could work together.

Within minutes of the modem being set up I was happily working away over VPN using Outlook and IM and everything else. It's nearly as fast as being in the office. My connection over VPN and not over VPN is clearly faster than before - it's also less prone to drop outs.

Long story short. It's a great router but don't expect it to fix everything. Make sure your modem is the most up to date both in terms of hardware and software too. Basically, any piece of anything between you and your internet could gum up the works and it's hard knowing where the issues is (router, modem, network card, etc.) I can't believe the number of well trained tech people I spoke to and not one of them questioned the modem. All of them seemed to think since I could get to the internet not over VPN that using VPN should make no difference. Clearly it did - apparently older modems don't play well with VPN.
text_fidelity_b: Cisco-Linksys WRT160N Wireless-N Broadband Router

text_fidelity_a: VIZIO M70-C3 70-Inch Class Ultra HD Full-Array LED Smart TV I really like this TV. So why 4 stars instead of 5? Well let me start with what is great about this TV and then we will get into why I dropped it a star. The price is amazing of course. I think back to the 42 inch Panasonic Plasma that I bought in 2002 and cringe at the multiple thousands spent. This is a lot of TV for the money. The picture is great. We have a 2012 59 inch top of the line Samsung Plasma and the picture on the Vizio is quite a bit sharper and brighter. It has replaced the Samsung as our go to Blue Ray movie night TV. So to this point we have a TV that is well priced and provides a great picture. So lets move on to the bad. Viewing angle. In our living room a couch sits directly in front of the Vizio. From the couch the picture is AMAZING. Off at about a 35 degree angle sits a recliner and the picture loses a lot of color, brightness and sharpness as viewed from the chair. It is not a horrible picture from the chair but it is quite a difference from straight on. The other is the somewhat slow response from the Vizio smart TV system. Compared to hooking up a Roku the initial start up and response is much slower. Of course if you are going to hook up a Roku then this is no big deal. If you do not have viewing angle concerns and are hooking up a Roku then I think you will absolutely love this amazing bargain.
text_fidelity_b: VIZIO M70-C3 70-Inch Class Ultra HD Full-Array LED Smart TV

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic HomeHawk Outdoor Wireless Smart Home Security Camera, Wide Angle View, Color Night Vision, 2-Way Talk, Works with Alexa & Google Assistant, 1 Camera Kit (KX-HN7001W) The Panasonic HomeHawk system has its good and its areas that could use some upgrades.
The good:
This is about as simple and install as you will get for a home monitoring system. No wires, five screws, charging the camera, downloading the app and you are ready to go, it is that simple. Once the cameras are charged and mounted I think it took me about 5 minutes to get everything running, and I am not technical by any stretch of the imagination.
The cameras are clear and provide good picture (you can select the quality of the picture when setting the system up) of the areas they are monitoring. Recordings are of good quality and clear, the night recording can be either color or black and white (infrared) depending on your choice.
Recording trigger areas can be set up along with sensitivity to movement in the recording area to trigger the recording to begin. All of these are very handy and easy to use.
The app is simple to use and pretty intuitive on how the system operates allowing almost everyone to use the system without any special knowledge. In all a good system for 95% of the people out there.
The things that can be improved.
It became apparent during setup of the outdoor camera (the one that looks like ET) that you need to mount it in a specific orientation, if you turn it over you cannot flip the image and everything will be upside down. If the ball neck for mounting the camera was just a little longer this would not be an issue as you could fit it under a soffit on your house wit a large field of view.
On the outdoor camera it works best when the rear of the camera is pointed in the direction of the base unit for connectivity. As you turn the camera and point the rear away from the base the signal drops pretty quick and the camera will not connect.
Other than these items the system is pretty easy to set up and use, now we see all the raccoons that show up to the house at night.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic HomeHawk Outdoor Wireless Smart Home Security Camera, Wide Angle View, Color Night Vision, 2-Way Talk, Works with Alexa & Google Assistant, 1 Camera Kit (KX-HN7001W)

text_fidelity_a:
Dell Inspiron 14 Plus 7420 Laptop - 14 inch, 2.2K 16:10, Intel Core i7-12700H, 16GB DDR5 RAM, 1TB SSD, Intel Iris Xe, 2 Yr Onsite + AntiVirus, Migrate, Windows 11 Pro+Office 365 - Atlantic Green This laptop computer is pretty much as advertised, and I am glad to have it. The screen is sharp and readable in 2240 x 1400 pixels mode. This model does NOT have a touch screen, so if that's important to you, you need to look at other laptops that sport that feature. The system so far is quick to respond to requests and has sufficient RAM and storage space.

One nice feature missing from all the other laptops I’ve owned or used is an automatic power up whenever the computer case is opened. There is also a power button in case you need it.

Beside Windows 11 Pro, this machine comes with significant value added: a year subscription to Microsoft Office 365 (normally $69.99/year) and also a two-year subscription to McAfee LiveSafe security suite (normally $129.99/year).

Most people who use laptops probably don’t mind that this machine, like most laptops now, does not have an ethernet port. However, WiFi seems to be performing well in its absence. I may not be the typical user, but I prefer the option to connect by ethernet.

I work almost exclusively at a desk with the power supply connected, so I have not tested the battery life of this Dell. My only real complaint is that, owing to the 14” display size, the keyboard is correspondingly smaller than I like. If I were to do much typing, I’d probably plug in an external keyboard. If your hands are smaller than mine are, this won't be much of an issue for you.

As has been mentioned in other reviews, this is not a gamer’s dream machine. It’s for normal office and business use. Its compact size makes it good for the road.
text_fidelity_b: Dell Inspiron 14 Plus 7420 Laptop - 14 inch, 2.2K 16:10, Intel Core i7-12700H, 16GB DDR5 RAM, 1TB SSD, Intel Iris Xe, 2 Yr Onsite + AntiVirus, Migrate, Windows 11 Pro+Office 365 - Atlantic Green

APC External Battery Pack, BR24BPG, Supplemental Battery for UPS Model BR1500G (Sold Separately) One of the main reasons I selected this model is the simplicity of a single battery cartridge design. My previous APC UPS units use spade connectors. I have limited use of my hands and fingers which makes it a challenge to use spade connectors so I was looking forward to the cartridge battery simplicity. When the product arrived I installed it as per the clear and easy to follow directions. But the UPS acted as if the battery was not connected and / or missing altogether. After spending a considerable time diagnosing the problem I finally removed the cartridge battery (Aaa-gain) to make a close inspection. I found there are two male blade connectors located within a pocket in the cartridge battery. Two female blade connectors are located in a protrusion inside the UPS unit battery compartment so as to self align and engage the male blades inside the pocket in the cartridge battery when the cartridge battery is installed and seated fully. One of the two male blade connectors is either missing or pressed in too deep to be reached by the mating coupling. I made a feeble attempt to tug at the stubby male blade sunk deep within the socket but gave up when I realized how stupid the situation is. This is a brand new product so why should I attempt to make a risky repair?

The problem as I see it is in attempting to get two flimsy electrical connectors to self align the first time every time all the time. If they had used common banana jacks instead of spade connectors it would only cost a penny more yet be so much more reliable.

As I write this I am awaiting a reply from APC. If APC will not take care of this problem then I will return my purchase to Amazon.com for a refund. I will follow up with the remedy after it is complete.
text_fidelity_b: APC External Battery Pack, BR24BPG, Supplemental Battery for UPS Model BR1500G (Sold Separately)

text_fidelity_a:
Kensington Wired SlimBlade Trackball Mouse (K72327U), Black I lived and breathed full-sized Kensington trackball mice from about 1987 until my last one stopped functioning and I couldn't find them anymore...probably in the late '90s. Tried some others; all had small, lightweight balls that gave none of the feel and control of Kensinton's...Expert Mouse? Was that what it was called back then too? Because it was the same general design as the current Expert Mouse, but the body was computer-case white.

Anyway, I had several of those (the quality going downhill with each iteration, as I recall) and loved them, and since they disappeared (as far as I could tell), I adapted, first to trackpads, which I've never liked much, and then back to traditional mice which don't give nearly the control of a trackball. Now, at last, it seems Kensington has again begun to produce truly worthwhile trackball mice, and this is one. Oh, it's _so_ good to have one of these again.

I'm doing that thing I hate when other people do it and reviewing the product as soon as I've gotten it up and running, without any kind of experiential history behind my assessment. I'll come back and update this in the future if necessary. But so far: I'm happy, happy, happy to have a real, full-sized Kensington trackball mouse again, with a heavy, substantial ball. There are only two things about this device that I'm not crazy about: In my old Kensington mice, the ball rested on physical rollers and I could give the ball a good spin and it would keep spinning for a second before stopping; it spun much more freely in its cavity than this ball does (so far...maybe that's something that will break in?) [Update: yes, after about three days of use the ball rolls more smoothly and silently than the old one on rollers ever did]. And the other thing is the scrolling mechanism. It's weird. Despite the KensingtonWorks software trying to make us believe otherwise, the "scroll ring" itself actually has nothing to do with scrolling, nor with anything else - the "scroll ring" is not even a control, but just a static piece of chrome trim. What makes the mouse scroll is twisting the ball this way or that from the top, as if it were a knob. At first I thought the "scroll ring" wasn't working because I was trying to use it without touching the ball...which does nothing. And now that I've figured out how scrolling works (you rest your finger on the "scroll ring" and push and pull the side of the ball)...I'm not crazy about it. I'm getting used to it, but it's just a weird way to scroll (I can't for the life of me remember how I used to do it on the Expert Mouse decades ago). It does work though.

(Update on the scrolling: I'm also not crazy about the way the KensingtonWorks software handles the scrolling speed adjustment. When you make the base pointer movement speed faster, the pointer continues to move smoothly, but just faster. When you make the scrolling speed faster though, you lose all smoothness - the software makes the scrolling faster by breaking it into successively larger and more jarring jumps. At the slowest speed, it's pretty smooth; at the highest speeds it's no longer really scrolling, but simply jumping abruptly from one screenful (or page) to the next. Increasing the scrolling speed just increases the size of these jumps, but I find them jarring and annoying starting at the second or third lowest speed setting.)

I also had to figure out how to program one of the buttons as a click lock, since Kensington doesn't call it that anymore, but calls it "left drag", "right drag", and "middle drag" (and I have no idea what the difference is between those three - I just chose "left drag" and it's working fine).

So far, those are my only gripes, all minor. So happy to have one of these things again! =) (Did I mention that?)

Enjoy...
text_fidelity_b: Kensington Wired SlimBlade Trackball Mouse (K72327U), Black

Wacom Bamboo Splash Pen Tablet (CTL471) Just a few days ago I finally decided it was time to give my old Genius 8x6 MousePen up. It was time to upgrade to a Wacom. I browsed for a day or two trying to decide what would best suit me, and after a lot of thought I decided this would be the tablet I purchased. It arrived the earliest day it said it would arrive, and that was a treat.

After I opened it up I thought this tablet would be too small since my other one was a bit bigger, but I tested it out in one of the programs that came with it, ArtRage Studio, and was very surprised. I barely realized the drawing space was small, and it was very comfortable and felt very natural to be drawing on. The tablet itself does not take up much space at all, and it's very light and small enough to be easy to work around. ArtRage Studio is also a very nice bonus. It's a great alternative to Photoshop and other programs (I actually see myself using this program more than my Photoshop). The Splash also came with three spare pen nibs for when your current one wears down.

The pen is also very nice in that it doesn't use batteries, and it also fits comfortably in your hand.

I am a little disappointed that this isn't compatible with a wireless connection, but the cord on the tablet really isn't that obtrusive.

I'm very happy with my very first Wacom product, and I hope I can upgrade once more in a few years.
text_fidelity_b: Wacom Bamboo Splash Pen Tablet (CTL471)

text_fidelity_a:
woednx Smart Watch,1.4''Full Touch Fitness Tracker with Heart Rate,Blood Pressure and Sleep Monitor,Message Notification,Smartwatch for Men WomenIP68 Waterproof Smartwatch Sports for iOS Android-Blue PROS

1. The silicone band is very comfortable. Apparently if it breaks, it can be replaced, though I’m not sure where or how you would buy a new band.

2. The appearance is sleek and modern, and the size of the watch face makes the digital numbers easy to read.

3. It has a rechargeable battery, which may have a longer life than the non-rechargeable batteries of most sports watches.

4. If you want a smart watch that is far cheaper than most brands, this might work for you.

CONS

1. There are three primary functions that I use a sports watch for: to instantly check the time, a stopwatch, and a timer. It irritated me no end with this watch that, after only a few seconds of being lit up, its face goes dark. While this might save the charge on the rechargeable battery, there are plenty of times when my right hand it not free to punch the button on this watch to light up its face, and I can’t quickly and conveniently check the time! It is also a hassle trying to use the stopwatch and timer functions.

2. I absolutely loathe the way this watch’s battery is recharged. Instead of using a standard C cable, the charging cable attaches magnetically, and it becomes detached far too easily. There is also no warning when the battery of this watch is about to go dead.

3. I don’t like the software this phone uses. It is a major hassle to learn for what I personally consider very little useful return. Why? Because most of the functions offered by this watch that are of any interest to me I can get through my smartphone. I use my phone and a Bluetooth for phone calls, texting, music, and hearing alarms. I check the weather by looking around me when outside or looking at weather apps on my phone. I use my phone for photography.
The rest of the functions this watch offers I personally find to be useless. I do not need a watch to tell me how to do a deep breathing exercises. As a healthy individual with no heart issues, I do not need to monitor my heart rate 24/7. (And if I did, I would use medical equipment that is far more reliable than this cheap watch.) I don’t need to obsessively monitor my sleep. (And, again, if I did, I wouldn’t trust this cheap watch to do an accurate job of it.)

4. Its pedometer function might have been of use to me, but unfortunately, it is inaccurate.

CONCLUSION

I dumped this watch and went back to a regular, inexpensive sports watch.
text_fidelity_b: woednx Smart Watch,1.4''Full Touch Fitness Tracker with Heart Rate,Blood Pressure and Sleep Monitor,Message Notification,Smartwatch for Men WomenIP68 Waterproof Smartwatch Sports for iOS Android-Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm Finepix F70EXR 10MP Super CCD Digital Camera with 10x Optical Dual Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7 inch LCD This is a high quality camera, but you must take time to read through the owner's manual to understand how to get the best pictures. You can just grab it and point and shoot using it while in the "automode" setting, but the resulting pictures may leave you a little disappointed depending upon the photographic conditions. To get the highest quality photos you must become familiar with how this little beauty works. Unfortunately, you might have to print out and tote the manual with you when you find yourself in situations where your pictures aren't what you'd like, or you can't figure out how to do certain things like know what's behind the flashing icon error message, or how to simulate different types of film, or can you choose between clarity, reduced noise and dynamic range? This is not really a simple "point and shoot" camera and all images will turn out great. You will have to study it, practice with it, and most of all have patience and you will be pleasantly rewarded for your efforts. Though the indicators vary with camera settings, there are 23 different indicators just for shooting mode, and 12 for playback mode, not to mention the date/time stamp, battery level, and indicator. It can get confusing.

Although a basic manual booklet is included with the camera, a much more detailed manual must be uploaded from the enclosed CD and then all 125 pages can be printed out or read from your computer monitor. The manual covers all the material in the booklet almost page for page but includes much more information about features the booklet leaves out and the booklet will refer you to specific pages in the manual for more information. Also, in the manual are about 50 FAQ's that are very useful. I am a manual reader, (having written many technical SOP's) and appreciate having well-written and well thought out manuals that are understandable and succinct. Though I would have preferred a manual that I don't have to upload to my computer, it is well-written and many useful pictures are included.

This camera is loaded with many different options/features but accessing and understanding many of them will require reading the manual. For people who don't want to be bothered with all the bells and whistles this camera may be more than they need. I can see very serious photographers using this camera. Reading through the manual I have compiled a list of some of the various modes, options and features available:

Digital Zoom
Movie Mode
Silent Mode
Variable ISO settings
Image size selection
Aspect Ratio selection
Intelligent Face detection
Scene Position
Shooting Modes
EXR Mode
Film simulation
Dynamic Range
White Balance
Continuous Photography
Photometry - multi, spot, average

Playback Options:
Erase
Slide Show
Red-eye Removal
Image Rotation
Protection from accidental deletion
Crop
Resize
Voice Memo
Print Order
Time Difference
Format

Pages 37, 67-68, 86-87, 97-103, and 104-107 would be good to print out and keep with your camera as they contain tables of various camera functions and a trouble shooting chart.

I have taken many pictures and movies inside and out, light and dark, with this camera set on various settings. And though I have practiced with it now for several weeks, I still need to often refer to the manual when I choose to vary from automode. Some things I have found especially desirable are:

Silent Mode - I attend classical music concerts where flash photography is prohibited. This mode will silence all beeps and flashes.

Large viewing screen on the back of the camera. It is exactly 5.5cm x 4.0 cm.

Digital Zoom - extremely good. I attended a local minor-league baseball game and sat far away on the grass well beyond the playing field. I was able to fully zoom and still get good, clear, close-up shots of the players with no blurring.

Movie Mode - Completely surpasses any other I've experienced so far. Images are clear, colorful and the sound quality is excellent. Camera noise was heard and recorded while using the "zoom" function in Movie Mode though it was not very loud.

Multi-frame play back function is very useful to quickly scan for a particular picture.

Fine Pix Viewer Program was very easy to install on my computer. I use Windows XP.

Very good photography in low-light conditions.

Also some things I did not find particularly desirable but are not major flaws:

I cannot directly burn a CD using the Fine Pix Viewer Program which comes with this camera. I have to use another camera program, import the pictures into it and then burn a CD.

Very easy to accidentally turn it on or off and easy to get misfires.

The zoom lever is too sensitive. I have learned with practice to barely move it very slowly.

The camera does not give helpful suggestions on how to get a better picture as does my HP R717.

Not HD capable.

The higher the ISO the grainier the picture though a higher ISO is desirable when shooting in dim/low light levels. I have set the ISO level to 200 and that seems to produce the best pictures so far.

Almost too many options, modes and functions to choose from. Though you can immediately begin to take pictures using Automode, it will take time to fully understand the many other aspects and features this camera has.

In Summary:

I can find no major complaint concerning this camera. It takes excellent clear and colorful photos even in situations where I least expect it - indoors with no flash. Any poor quality pictures I have taken are not the fault of the camera but due to the photographer's ignorance of how to use/understand properly the many features of the camera. The basic mechanics of such things as battery and memory card installation are very easy. Battery charging is a very simple process and battery life seems long. The manual is detailed and covers more than I would probably care to know. This is almost more camera than I need, though I will continue to use it and will update this review as necessary.

UPDATE 2.9.15 - Been using this camera all these years and now it's beginning to show it's age and giving me some problems. The viewing screen on the back has a vertical big black bar but it doesn't appear on the actual pictures. And the lens cover doesn't always completely open when the camera is turned on. I still use it but it might be time to think about a replacement. It's been good though so I really don't have any complaints.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Finepix F70EXR 10MP Super CCD Digital Camera with 10x Optical Dual Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7 inch LCD

Amazfit BIP smartwatch by Huami with all-day heart rate & activity tracking, sleep monitoring, GPS, 30-day battery life, Bluetooth (Kokoda Green), One Size June 7, 2018—This watch, an Amazfit Bip smartwatch, arrived today so I'm posting an initial review about it. I come back after some time and change or add anything that needs it.
----------------------------------
Amended June 15, 2018
I have downgraded the Amazfit Bip Smartwatch from 5-Stars to 1-Star. This is why:
1) My Pixel 2 updated to Android 8.1, the watch unpaired in the process and now will not reconnect (pair with) the phone.
2) Nothing in Amazfit's on-line support addresses this issue. However, there are a significant number of Bip owners discussing this problem on the internet, outside of Amazfit's site.
3) The watch is not a useless brick and exchanging texts with Amazfit's tech support is not going to get this fixed (if at all) in a timely enough manner for my purposes.
4) Finally, I got 7 1/2 days service from this watch and that is very poor, indeed.

Sorry to say, my opinion is the Bip does NOT WORK WITH ANDROID 8.1. That seemingly the case, what will happen when Android P, now in Beta, releases as Android 9 in August, 2018?

I'm going back to my iPhone/Apple Watch. Yes, that combination has glitches as well. However, support for Apple Products is always reliable and you're not stuck texting for help.

I have a few different hubs now because Apple decided I only needed USB-C ports on my laptop. Depending on what I’m doing and how many devices I need to plug in, I’ll either use a hub or adapters.

WiFi signal strength can be impacted by hubs or similar devices, there’s some interference with USB 3.0 and 2.4Ghz networks. It’s a known problem, there’s a lot about it online if you’ve also run into it. I’ve noticed this using other hubs, and I have about the same degree of interference with this one.

I don’t love the design of this hub. I wish the hub’s USB-C plug was straight, not an “L.” While I can still plug in other USB-C things next to the hub, the “L” shape of the plug dictates how the hub sits on my desk.

The hub is bigger than it needs to be. Maybe if the glassy front was repurposed, the USB 3.0 ports laid out in a square rather than a line, it wouldn’t take up as much room on my desk. The big display only has a tiny icon to show me when the hub is on … I just don’t like the wasted space.
text_fidelity_b: Baseus USB-C Docking Station, USB C Data Hub Adapter with PD Type C Charging Port, 5-in-1 USB C Dongle Adapter for MacBook/Pro/Air 2018,Chromebook,XPS,Galaxy S10/S9/S8/Note9

text_fidelity_a:
Olympus VN-541PC digital voice recorder with one-touch recording, noise-cancellation function, 4GB memory, four scenes recording, includes a micro-USB cable. This is a nice light-weight (2.4 ounces) basic voice recorder that comes in handy to record small messages or “to do” things when I am driving to work or on vacation. I generally spend an hour driving to work each way and when I remember certain “to do” things, then I record on this little gadget and replay it when I am home. I have also used this device to record hour long meetings in small a conference room at work and also music (mono) from YouTube. The music quality is acceptable and the playback of the voice recordings are also acceptable. The operation is very easy and the instruction manual is helpful in guiding through the process if you are stuck.

This machine runs on two AAA size batteries and comes with a USB cable that connects to a laptop or any device that has USB port. The device appears as a separate drive, just click on it and you can see the fours recording scene options; “Memo” or “Talk.” “Music and “LP”. I usually use “Memo” or “Talk” for recording small messages and the “Music” option for music scene, “LP” scene for long recordings. You can cut/copy the files you want to save and paste onto your laptop or any other device you have connected with this recorder. It will also free up the space on the recorder. The files could also be copied to other USB drives. The recorder has a total 506 hours of space for recordings.

The con is that is it doesn’t have a microSD card slot, which could have been helpful to listen to some quality music. The USB cable is very short. While recording, the light doesn’t blink as the recording devices commonly do. The voice-strength (volume) is weak, and it doesn't have an internal battery which could have been charged by plugging into the main outlet, instead it uses only two AAA batteries.
text_fidelity_b: Olympus VN-541PC digital voice recorder with one-touch recording, noise-cancellation function, 4GB memory, four scenes recording, includes a micro-USB cable.

text_fidelity_a:
Apple AirPods Pro Long story short I lost my airpod pros. Saw these on major discount ($90 for Black Friday), and couldn't resist. So here's my take in four parts. Sound Quality. Noise Cancelling. Ambient pass through. Features.

Sound quality -- versus the airpod pros, these are almost identical in sound. The only difference is the beats buds are a touch bass heavy. It's good, punchy bass, but noticeably more than the pros which were more balanced with its lows. So if you're a bass head, or hip-hop enthusiast, the beats win hands down.

Noise cancelling -- now this could have to do with the shape of my ear, but I found the beats to actually be a step ABOVE in noise cancelling. My gf still has her airpods and I compared. The seal the beat creates, paired with its noise cancelling makes it seem like the world doesn't exist. Beats win for me in NC.

Ambient pass-through -- this is where the beats lose out. Their noise cancelling is too good. So even when you have transparency turned on the world sound a little muddied out, while with the airpods, if I had transparency on it was almost like I wasn't wearing them. I miss that alot. So if you are in an environment where you need to hear what people are saying without removing your buds then airpods might be your pick. It's not to say that beats mak you deaf or anything but things are just noticeably quieter in transparance vs airpods with its full clarity.

Features -- another loss for the beats. They don't work with the beats app so no equalizer function... why beats???? WHY?? So you'll have to go third party if you want to equalize. The beats also won't stop the music or video you're watching if one falls out. No biggy for me as I like that but some people might not. Other than that it has similar functionality to airpods. One click to pause, two to skip, etc. It doesn't auto switch between devices but does actually switch pretty similarly. Takes maybe two clicks to switch it to my mac. The pairing is a breeze with iphones. Just open the case next to your iphone and voila. It's paired.
text_fidelity_b: Apple AirPods Pro

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Chromebook, 11.6-Inch, CB3-111-C670 (Intel Celeron, 2GB, 16GB SSD, White) **Discontinued by Manufacturer** I'm typing this review on this Chromebook right now! I'm a graduate student, and I got tired of my Windows computer installing updates every time I opened my laptop. It was frustrating. I just wanted to open my laptop and get right to writing my homework. Now I can! It's also very lightweight, so I can easily bring it and all my books with me to class. It holds a charge for at least 2-3 days of active homework use and general internet fun for me. It starts up almost instantly when I open it! The screen size is fine, and I often have two windows open at the same time, side by side. I've been trying to read more articles online without printing them, and using online textbooks via my Kindle app. After a bit of a learning curve, this has worked out awesome, because if I have my Chromebook, I have ALL my textbooks with me, plus my course information, and my notebook to write things down. I love it. Plus, it doesn't get hot or make a whirring sound when you use it for a long time. I like that because I often use mine while I"m sitting on the couch.

Getting used to using the Chromebook had some hiccups. First, I recommend using Google Docs for writing because it has an offline mode. The Windows OneDrive and cloud version of Word works ok, but if your internet has any interruption, you can't keep typing. That's annoying. So use Google Docs, and don't worry about it! (But if you're working on a project with someone, and they use Word on a Windows laptop, you can collaborate with them no problem using the cloud version of Word.) Second, organizing my files confused me, until I realized that "Save As" is now "Move to folder.' Also, you can download a few files to your Chromebook, so if you need to upload an attachment to Blackboard, you can pretty easily. You'll use your Google Drive for much of your file storage. I did connect my OneDrive to my Chromebook, but it's through a third party app thing, and the connection always has to be redone, so I don't really rely on that, and I plan to move my OneDrive stuff to my Google drive soon.

The only thing that was really hard was setting up my Chromebook to print to my WiFi printer. Google cloud print is in beta, and in theory, it's awesome. When you're done setting it up, you could print to your home printer from anywhere, using your mobile device. However, Google your printer and how to set up cloud print, and give yourself some time to set it up. If you're in a rush, you should just plug your printer into your Chromebook.

Lastly, since many public schools are going Chromebook, I thought it was a good idea to get one myself. I'm working on getting my Master of Arts in Teaching to be an elementary/middle school teacher. Using one for my own schoolwork helps me be able to help students use their Chromebooks. Additionally, the price is so nice, I don't worry about having to ever replace my Chromebook, because if it was damaged by schoolchildren, I'd only be out about $160 (instead of $2000 for a Mac). I'm even thinking of getting one for my mom, since most of what she does online could be done on a Chromebook, too.

Oh, and one very last thing, the keyboard is really enjoyable to type on. The keys are spaced comfortably, and the individual keys make a nice clicky sound, are springy, and are nice and thin, for fast typing. I know that might sound weird, but I'm picky about my keyboards.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook, 11.6-Inch, CB3-111-C670 (Intel Celeron, 2GB, 16GB SSD, White) **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

text_fidelity_a:
Contour +2 - Old Packaging (Discontinued by Manufacturer) UPDATE: Local retailer slashed prices and a buddy bought a new +2 (new packaging) and found : new packaging doesn't come with HDMI cable, or the external mic adaptor. He promptly returned it and got an "old packaging" and now had all the equipment. Why the "new packaging" costs more than the "old packaging" is beyond me. The "new packaging" mimics the Roam2 packaging, with no see thru "bubble" at the top of the box - BEWARE!!!

FYI - BB discontinuing the Contour line and the mounts are all 50% off, and the camera(s) are $100 off.

This is a dual review, as I own both the Contour + 2 and the Contour Roam2. I don't work for nor do I have any affiliation with Contour. I've had the Roam2 for more than 6 months, but held off writing this review until I had the +2 to compare it to. Although I don't own a GoPro, several friends do and I do their video editing so I'll chime in on the Contour vs. GoPro at the end.

MOUNTS:
Contour uses the same proprietary mounts across their lineup, so interchangeability between the two should be fairly easy (but doesn't always work out that way). I've found some to be flimsy(hat mount), while others are damn near bomb proof(suction cup)! The rotating lens means you can mount it in just about any position, however it is difficult to know that you've framed the shot with the correct orientation! Had an important video recorded upside down - laser level only lets you know it's level, not if it's upside down! One of the best features I've found is the ¼ by 20 thread on the bottom of the Contour, pretty much universal to all modern cameras and there's a TON of mounts out there reasonably priced.

SOFTWARE:
The Storyteller program needs to be installed on your computer and is fairly easy to use, but not intuitive, you need to play around a bit before you can figure everything out. The editing ability is extremely limited. (I use imovie). Software is free, and although you can use the camera(s) without first updating I suggest you do that first! The +2 also has an app that I use on my iPhone 5 - it too is free and pretty easy to use - but not as capable as the Storyteller program. The downside is you HAVE to use the Storyteller program to change settings on the Roam2, AND you have to use it if you want to use any of the GPS data with the +2.

ROAM2:
Got this for Xmas last year and immediately swapped the included 4GB micro SD for a 16GB. SUPER easy to use - charge, point, and slide the slider to the on position. Video quality is good, first few outings I had it set for 1080@30 and was very happy. In editing I found one clip I had to slow down and was slightly disappointed at the quality - since then I've got it set for 720@60 and haven't had any issues - video quality is still good (even in slow mo). Low light does induce more "noise" to the video, but if there's ambient light (streetlights etc.) you can still get decent vids. Sound quality isn't all that, it's usable, but in high winds or at speed - forget it. Battery life is really good at around 2 hours. The camera itself is very well built, one of my first uses it got throw (by an idiot) about 8ft into about 4 inches of water over concrete - few scratches, but still kept recording. This led me to look for something to help protect the aluminum body - Glock Tape, works amazing, adds some protection, but most importantly gives it some GRIP!

[[ASIN:B00C7WXTJS 6-Pack Glock Grip Tape - Pistol Grip Tape. * Use on handguns and rifles * Not gritty like sandpaper or skateboard tape. * Does not scuff clothing, holsters, furniture or car seats like those sandy tapes. * Makes chambering a round easier for arthritis s...]]

CONTOUR +2:
Only had it for a week or so, really wanted it due to the Bluetooth (to help frame shots) and was wanted the waterproof housing (worried about watersports damage on an upcoming trip) the GPS would be a plus. Once again amazing build quality - this things tough as nails. First thing I did was hook up to Storyteller and get the latest firmware update - less than 5 minutes later I was off and running! Pairing the Bluetooth took a couple of attempts, but once connected has excellent range (20 or so feet with obstructions - close to 50ft line of sight!). Using the app you can check status of battery, GPS, and memory as well as change settings and start stop recording - wish you could watch videos but oh well. The app has about a one second delay between what the camera "sees" and what you see on your phone - pretty amazing! Attached to my suction cup mount and went for a drive - took about 30 seconds for the GPS to lock on the first time (since then it only takes maybe 5 seconds). GPS is accurate. The video quality is great! Uploaded vid into storyteller and the GPS data was also great - until I exported it then there was a lag of about 5 seconds between the data being displayed and the video. Waterproof housing is bulky, yet seems a bit flimsy - still not sure it could survive 200 ft of water. Came with HDMI to hook up to TV - works really well. Haven't used the mic adaptor yet. Battery life seems to be around 1.5 hours, but spare batteries are cheap.

[[ASIN:B007PUC1UU Wasabi Power Battery and Charger Kit for Contour 2350, 2450, 2900, C010410K and ContourHD, ContourGPS, Contour+, Contour+2]]

COMPARISON:
Even though the video specs are the same between the +2 and the Roam2, the video quality of the +2 is noticeably better - even in low light. Sound quality on both suffers in high winds or speed. They both have the proprietary T-rail mounts on both sides, but the ¼ by 20 thread is about an inch further back on the +2. The Roam2 is waterproof without housing to about 3ft, but the +2 has the waterproof housing. The +2 also allows for filming while charging. The +2 has the HDMI out, as well as a jack for external mic. The +2 has the Bluetooth app, plus GPS - that combined with replaceable batteries and the better video make it worth the extra money.

CONTOUR vs. GOPRO:
I absolutely love the form factor and the mounting options available for the Contours. The Contour line has their own proprietary mounts, but the ability to use the ¼ by 20 thread mounts for other cameras (even the GoPro mounts) plus the rotating lens means there's just more ways to mount the Contour. That being said the GoPro Hero3 flat out destroys the video quality of the Roam2, and slightly edges out the +2. Of course this difference (even over the Roam2) is completely removed once video is uploaded to Youtube or other sharing sites as they compress the video during upload! I've yet to see a GoProH3 recording 1080 go for more than 75 minutes. Sound quality between all three is about the same. The GoProH3 app uses wifi - and has about a 3-4 second delay - still works for framing shots, but not much else. The GoPro also has the advantage in that you can change settings in camera - but it is a complicated affair(the +2 only allows you to choose between two predetermined settings). GoProH3 doesn't have GPS, or rotating lense. Contour recently lowered the price on the +2 it's now $50 cheaper than the GoProH3. Also it seems they changed pricing on their mounts - I went with the Contour line because of the simplicity of their system, more mounts, cheaper price, and the form factor. Now that they're cheaper it's a no brainer.
text_fidelity_b: Contour +2 - Old Packaging (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech M705 Marathon Wireless Mouse – Long 3 Year Battery Life Ergonomic Sculpted Right-Hand Shape Hyper-Fast Scrolling and USB Unifying Receiver for Computers and laptops Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer) UPDATE (3/30/2019):

This mouse is still functioning as when it was new. I have replaced my 10-year-old Mac Pro with the 2018 Mac mini. I am still using the original Apple Cinema Display. The Logitech Control Center app was installed so the M705 / Marathon mouse would function properly. From time to time I have to unplug the unifying receiver and reinsert it to regain full access to the mouse and its correct assignments of the buttons.

NOTE: There is a newer version of the M705 mouse that does NOT have the side button (left side next to the thumb). The price I paid was $20 recently, but I have not used the newer version yet since this one that HAS the side button still functions.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (November 13, 2017 ):

This mouse was bought to replace the 4-year-old Logitech Performance Mouse - rechargeable battery - because the mouse acted erratically due to lint and other debris that got into the space between the bottom and the plastic covers over the buttons. It prevented drag-and-drop when it would disconnect while dragging. Sometimes the file being moved ended up in another folder that meant I had to UNDO the move and start over. What a pain.

(I began buying Logitech mouse designs after spending too much - $80 - for the Microsoft M6000 laser mouse that was terrible.)

The duration of the parallel battery design makes it last a longer time - I have not had to replace the original batteries yet, but I have been using this only since March of this year (8 months).

The pointer has a tendency to become up to 5 times larger if I move the mouse quickly back and forth left and right. I don't know if this is the mouse or the computer software. I find this interesting, but it does not concern me so I have not asked if anyone else has had the same experience.

One star has been deducted because the scrolling wheel can be used to move up or down the window I am viewing but the window jumps back to where I started. It does not do this all the time, but when I want to scroll up or down to see what has been displayed, it is a pain to have it jump back down or up to where the page had been.

The weight of the mouse is irrelevant when one uses the mouse. It stays on the mouse pad / surface just fine. I am not sure why someone would object to having a second battery in this mouse. For those who have forgotten any high school physical science, the parallel arrangement maintains the 1.5 volts of a single battery but doubles the capacity / run-time of one battery.

As for the mouse specifications: (height x width x depth): 2.6 x 4.3 x 1.6 in; 70.0 x 109.0 x 40 mm (these are from the Logitech site; I would say these measurements are width x length x height considering the way it usually is positioned). Mouse weight: 4.8 oz; 135 g. Compatible OS: Windows 7, Windows 8, Windows 10, Windows XP, Windows Vista, Mac OS X 10.5 or later, Chrome OS.

For anyone who needs a wireless full-size mouse, I recommend the Logitech M705.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech M705 Marathon Wireless Mouse – Long 3 Year Battery Life Ergonomic Sculpted Right-Hand Shape Hyper-Fast Scrolling and USB Unifying Receiver for Computers and laptops Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
