Denon D-M41 Home Theater Mini Amplifier and Bookshelf Speaker Pair - Compact HiFi Stereo System with CD, FM/AM Tuner and Wireless Bluetooth Music | Perfect for Small Rooms and Home Cinema It was time to upgrade my home stereo. I've had it for decades, and I also needed a CD player. After a bunch of research, I settled on this as a solution. Moving from a full-sized receiver and larger speakers to this was actually fairly refreshing. Here are some thoughts:

Build quality
Everything felt solid when taking it out of the box. The speakers also had a nice heft. The remote felt great, too. Once I got it set up, all the buttons had a nice feel, the volume knob was smooth, and the CD tray opened/closed in a very smooth fashion. Taking a look at the back, you have all the connections you'll need for most purposes.

Sound
I was VERY impressed at how clear this thing is. It's my first "HiFi" system, and a huge improvement over the old Aiwa/Bose system that I had. When I was gearing up to buy this, I figured I might need a small subwoofer to provide a bit of low frequency support. That's not the case at all for music! These little speakers pump out rich and full sound. I may still invest in a small sub for movies, however.

CD/Bluetooth
My primary uses for this will be for music. The CD player handles all my CDs just fine (including the "enhanced" CDs that my previous players failed to play.) Connecting this to my phone was a snap, and the Bluetooth audio sounded just fine (for Bluetooth.)

Overall, this is a little powerhouse of a system, and I can't be happier.
text_fidelity_b: Denon D-M41 Home Theater Mini Amplifier and Bookshelf Speaker Pair - Compact HiFi Stereo System with CD, FM/AM Tuner and Wireless Bluetooth Music | Perfect for Small Rooms and Home Cinema

text_fidelity_a:
Plantronics BackBeat PRO Wireless Noise Canceling Hi-Fi Headphones with Mic - Compatible with iPhone, iPad, Android, and Other Smart Devices I would, that I could give these headphones a zero-star rating. As I don’t think they deserve a whole star. When I was in school, a gold star meant something. And these headphones are not deserving of such.
Ok, on with the bad. My first set of these. If I would whipe the sweat out of my left ear. Left ear specifically, as the right ear did not produce this effect. The sound would cut off. Not the little off, then on again. As the phones shut off when you take them off your head. So a little off then on, would be expected. But I mean off, and stay that way. Then you need to turn off the headphones, with the switch, and back on again.
Which leads to the second problem. The phones cannot reconnect after the connection has been broken. The computer will blue screen, and restart. I thought, well maybe it is the Bluetooth receiver. So I got a new one, by a different company. Same issue.
Problem three. None of the buttons work. The buttons I am referring to are the play, pause, track forward, or track backward.
And it really makes me sad, to say these bad things about these phones. And I really tried to blame something other things at fault, to save their face. Because they have the most awesome form factor I can find in a headphone. The buttons are so intuitively placed, even if they do not work. The design, is obviously a different department. And the volume, is not controlled by a buttons. But rather a good old analog type knob. And the sound quality is pretty good, and also the noise cancelling works.
Oh yeah, I almost forgot. Because I really like the form factor. I thought I should give them another chance. So I replaced this set, with another set of the same model. And had the same problems. Evey, single, one, of them.

I had to take apart one of my drives in an enclosure just to move the files over after using an image actually worked.

So this is for when you want to use a internal drive externally but not on a regular basis, such as cloning the drive and then exchanging the drive into another or the same computer. I am a heavy user of my computer and hard drives only last so long. This is a very useful tool and very easy to use. I used it to move some additional files that got missed during the initial transfer and it worked well. It was immediately recognized by the computer. The transfer rates are consistent with USB 3.0. I have used Sabrent enclosures for years and found them to be consistent, so I expect this will too. It may require more gentle handling than an actual enclosure, but it isn't made for constant use - i.e. your drive will have no protection while using it, so it is not a long term solution. But I could see a computer repair person using it on a constant basis on multiple drives. I think if you are careful in the plugging in and unplugging, it should last for years.

CHUWI Hi8 8 inch Windows 10/Android 4.4 Dual Boot Tablet PC, with Features of Intel Quad Core, Full HD 19201200 IPS Screen, 2G RAM/32G ROM and Winkey Price is one thing that's good about this tablet. I have no problem with the cheap plastic all around (really, it almost felt like a disposable food tray), considering the price tag, but there were a couple of things I just couldn't get over.

- Whatever Android OS is installed here, it came without Google Play app. Once I installed it myself, it crashed every time I tried to download a new app from Google app store. This is unacceptable, especially considering that the tablet comes with almost no apps to begin with.
-By the time I updated Windows & set up tablet, it was already getting uncomfortable warm. I can't imagine what would happen if I tried doing something like taping a video for an hour.
- USB socket was loose, I had to jiggle the cable several times to get it charging, and a smallest shift caused it to disconnect again.
- I expected pretty poor camera from the specs, but this was outstanding. Video & images had all the charm and quality of those tiny snapshots from the early mobile phones. Made me kind of nostalgic, but I expect better from a current tablet.

Unrelatedly to the quality of tablet itself, I'm glad I got to try a Windows 10 OS tablet on a dual boot machine, so I know to avoid it from now on... a clumsy hybrid of desktop and tablet capabilities. Android booted and run reasonably fast, while Win 10 lagged on the same machine.

I'm returning it.
text_fidelity_b: CHUWI Hi8 8 inch Windows 10/Android 4.4 Dual Boot Tablet PC, with Features of Intel Quad Core, Full HD 19201200 IPS Screen, 2G RAM/32G ROM and Winkey

SleepPhones AcousticSheep Classic | Corded Headphones for Sleep, Travel, and More | The Original and Most Comfortable Headphones for Sleeping | Soft Gray - Fleece Fabric (Size M) I suffer from tinnitus and listen to white noise or meditation videos on YouTube while trying to sleep--otherwise the ringing is just too distracting. I have been using earbuds for the past two years, but for various reasons no longer wish to use them. So I ordered SleepPhones, hoping they would eliminate the need for uncomfortable ear buds.

I have tried these for two nights in a row. Both nights I woke up with the cord around my neck; the band had shimmied to the top of my head (read: speakers not where they need to be); and I was sweating from the fleece (maybe I need to wait to review until the temperature has dipped below 80 degrees where I live). Plus, the speakers only offer any significant volume when my phone volume is turned on high--even then, I wish I could get it a bit higher.

I was really hoping these would be a good alternative to earbuds, but I think I will continue to be disappointed and am out $35...

text_fidelity_a:
Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch This is a retro leather laptop messenger bag - the material is made from something called "Buffalo" leather, which feels rough and stiff - quite the opposite of lambskin or buttery soft leather. The buckles are only for show because you can open and close the bag without unbuckling it, as there are buttons underneath. It has a weathered look, with varying shades of brown and sienna that give the impression that you're an Indiana Jones-type adventurer who's been carrying this bag through the outback, escaped tigers and bears, and came through fine, though the bag is a bit battered.

In other words, it's very manly, and harks back to the 1940s when bulky items were the norm because thinner materials hadn't been invented yet. While it looks great and seems well made (it's from India), it's actually limited in terms of actual everyday use. If you're traveling a lot, you want things to be as lightweight as possible. This is not one of those items. Even when empty, it feels cumbersome to carry. Stuffed with a laptop and papers, it will be heavy.

Think about it - when was the last time you actually saw someone on the train or airport carrying one of these? You might say you'd like to do so because it will make you look unique. In reality, other people may have tried carrying one of these and gave up.

So while it's nice as a conversation piece and something you might want to show off to your friends, I fear it will be one of those novelty items that, after its newness has worn off, will be relegated to the back of the closet.
text_fidelity_b: Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag Office Briefcase College Bag Fits Upto 14 Inch

HP Sprocket Portable Color Photo Printer, Print Social Media Photos on 2x3" Sticky-Backed Paper - Black (X7N08A) This is a great improvement over an earlier-gen ZINK paper ("zero ink") portable printer we have, which requires a wired connection and a proprietary charger, and no longer holds a charge well.

The HP Sprocket connects and prints wirelessly, charges from a standard micro-USB cable, and has a lithium-ion battery which is sure to last a lot longer.

We had it unboxed and printing in less than 5 minutes. You run it from a free app available for Android or Apple iOS devices. We used the Android version and it works great.

It takes less than 30 seconds to wirelessly send and print a photo. The prints are 2 inches by 3 inches, smooth and glossy, good resolution, and have a peel-and-stick backing for quick and easy mounting. In the long run, the priciest thing about a ZINK printer is the paper, so shop around for deals.

The prints came out a little to the warm side in color when sent "as is," but the app allows a lot of enhancement and has lots of effects you can add.

The Sprocket printer itself measures only 3 inches by 5 inches and less than an inch thick, and weighs about 6-and-a-half ounces. It's very portable.

And it's loads of fun.
text_fidelity_b: HP Sprocket Portable Color Photo Printer, Print Social Media Photos on 2x3" Sticky-Backed Paper - Black (X7N08A)
